moves.headline: Nvidia jumps 31% after its board reinstates Jensen Huang as chief executive
moves.summary: Nvidia rose 31.5% to $165.05, its biggest one-day gain in years, after the board reinstated co-founder Jensen Huang as president, chief executive and director with immediate effect, eleven days after he resigned.
why: Huang resigned on November 12 after reports of relationships with employees and with an executive at Megaspeed suspected of being a Chinese agent, and the shares lost almost half their value from their October high in the turmoil that followed. Before Monday’s open the board reversed course: it said it had received input from senior levels of the US government and concluded that his return poses no national security risk. President Trump had publicly urged the board to bring him back and praised the decision.

The board said its independent investigation into Huang’s ties to the Megaspeed executive will proceed to its conclusion, and it formed a new National Security and Export Control Committee. Investors took the decision as removing the largest single uncertainty over the company, but the SEC’s reported investigation into Nvidia’s disclosures and the political scrutiny of chip sales to China are still open.
context: US stocks had their best day since April 2025 on November 23. The Nasdaq rose close to 7% during the session and the S&P 500 about 5%, recovering much of the previous week’s sell-off, in which chip stocks had their worst week since 2001.
More than 120 US companies worth over $2 billion rose 10% or more on the day, almost all of them chipmakers, memory makers, data-centre suppliers and other AI-linked stocks.

src.title: Stocks post best day since April 2025 as Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang (Yahoo Finance)

moves.headline: Nvidia falls 14% as the AI sell-off deepens amid an SEC probe and leadership turmoil
moves.summary: Nvidia shares fell 14.0% to $125.53, leading a rout in chip stocks that sent the Nasdaq down 5.3%. The company is dealing with the resignation of co-founder Jensen Huang, a reported SEC investigation of its disclosures and political scrutiny over chip sales to China.
why: Nvidia has been at the centre of a month-long sell-off in AI stocks. Co-founder and chief executive Jensen Huang resigned on November 11–12 after an internal investigation into his personal conduct, ending more than three decades at the helm. On November 17 The Wall Street Journal reported that the SEC had opened a civil investigation into whether Nvidia’s disclosures misled investors, and US officials including Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent have publicly questioned whether the company knowingly sold advanced chips to China.

Nvidia reported quarterly results above expectations on November 17, but the shares kept falling as investors focused on the governance questions, new US limits on AI chip exports and data-centre expansion abroad, rising bond yields and broader doubts about the financing of the AI build-out. On November 20 the selling became indiscriminate across chipmakers, memory makers and data-centre suppliers, and Nvidia’s 14% drop erased hundreds of billions of dollars of market value in a single session.
context: On November 20 the Nasdaq Composite fell 5.3% and the S&P 500 3.7%, pushing the S&P 500 and the Dow into correction territory and wiping out the Nasdaq’s gain for 2026. Semiconductors led the fall, capping their worst week since 2001.

Nvidia has now fallen almost 48% from its record close of $239.24 on October 6. At around 13 times trailing earnings it is valued far below its average of recent years, but the outcome of the SEC probe, the board’s choice of a permanent chief executive and any new export restrictions are open questions that the market is pricing as serious risks.
